hunt.justification: Adversaries scale identity attacks by renting legitimate infrastructure that standard risk scoring cannot distinguish from normal traffic. This hunt provides the manual oversight needed to identify these clusters across a fleet.

meta.name: Abuse of Clean Hosting Infrastructure for Identity Attacks

related.reason: This hunt focuses on the infrastructure origin (hosting providers), while the sibling hunt focuses on the protocol mechanics across all IP ranges.

meta.analysis: A simple detection rule on these IP ranges would produce too many false positives for legitimate developers. We use a gated flow to first confirm successful logins, then stack protocols for rarity, and finally correlate with host-side connections to differentiate between a developer and an adversary.

scenario.summary: Attackers utilize clean hosting infrastructure and AI-generated phishing lures to conduct high-volume identity attacks against Microsoft 365 tenants. These campaigns involve device-code phishing and password spraying via legacy ROPC flows to bypass MFA and harvest session tokens for replay through German hosting relays.

meta.rationale: The lead query focuses on successful logins from documented hosting clusters. If the initial lead results in high volume, use the scope_hosts parameter to focus the network connection correlate step on the most active beachhead machines.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary uses trusted developer or cloud hosting platforms to bypass identity risk scoring, using legacy protocols (ROPC) or Device Code Flow to steal or replay session tokens.

hunt.name: Abuse of Clean Hosting Infrastructure for Identity Attacks
hunt.description: This hunt targets the use of clean cloud infrastructure, specifically Railway and 1337 Services GmbH ranges, to host AiTM relays and execute password sprays. Attackers use these platforms because they have high IP reputation, causing standard Entra ID risk scoring to ignore them. The hunt starts by identifying successful sign-ins from these known malicious hosting ranges, then fans out to analyze the prevalence of specific auth protocols (ROPC, Device Code Flow) and corroborates with endpoint-side network connections to the same infrastructure.

nodes.label: Prevalence of Legacy and MFA-Skipping Protocols

config.content: SELECT auth_protocol, src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS user_count, COUNT(*) AS login_attempts FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE instr(',' || '{{legacy_protocols}}' || ',', ',' || auth_protocol || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY auth_protocol, src_endpoint_ip HAVING user_count <= 3 ORDER BY user_count ASC, login_attempts DESC
config.description: Detect rare IPs that use ROPC or DeviceCode flow.
config.expected_signal: Rare IP addresses that use ROPC or DeviceCode flow against a limited number of users.

nodes.label: Revoke Sessions and Force Password Change

config.description: Immediately invalidate the adversary's access tokens and prevent further sign-ins.
config.instructions: Revoke all active sessions for the identified user accounts and force a password reset immediately.

config.description: Review follow-on activity using active voice instructions.
config.instructions: Inspect hb_cloud_api_activity for the compromised users. ensure the adversary did not establish persistence by looking for New-InboxRule or Update-MfaDevice. identify calls the adversary made after the initial sign-in from the malicious range.

config.description: Document result and update parameters for the next run.
